workflows.name: Calibrated photos and controls to editable CAD
workflows.output_scope: Metric-anchored camera solution, dense surface reference and constrained CAD interpretation.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Multi-view photos with adequate overlap and stable exposure; at least ten diverse calibration-target views if using the OpenCV calibration route; explicit scale/control measurements; dense MVS and selected OCS feature modeling.

inputs.format_and_quality: JPG/PNG originals with camera metadata; sharp overlapping views and visible calibration board in calibration subset.
JSON/CSV target dimensions and 3D control coordinates with units, plus named image-pixel correspondences or board measurements.
Text naming components, datums and intended CAD feature scope; it supplies semantics, not dimensions.

workflows.reference_points: Board corners: object coordinates in target frame and pixel detections. Calibration target establishes intrinsics and target-frame units; camera calibration alone does not scale the object capture. At least two separated measured scale/control distances are used to set/check reconstruction scale; reserve one or more controls from fitting. COLMAP adapter detail: OpenCV pixel-center principal point is shifted +0.5 px in x and y for COLMAP; OpenCV’s five coefficients [k1,k2,p1,p2,k3] map into COLMAP FULL_OPENCV [k1,k2,p1,p2,k3,k4,k5,k6] with the final three set to zero. Verify COLMAP camera database readback after feature extraction. COLMAP bundle adjustment refines parameters by default unless controlled; choose this based on calibration evidence.

software.name: OpenCV
software.licence_scope: Apache-2.0 for OpenCV >=4.5 (including current 4.x); older releases retain their release-specific BSD-3-Clause terms

software.name: COLMAP / pycolmap
software.role_and_api: feature extraction, matching, mapper; CLI or pycolmap

software.name: OCS
software.role_and_api: Existing OCS session controls and constrained CAD readback

software.name: AliceVision Meshroom alternate
software.role_and_api: meshroom_batch --input <image-folder> --output <output-folder> invokes the documented photogrammetry pipeline; `--save <project.mg>` persists the graph. This route manages its own graph and calibration; it does not consume the OpenCV calibration JSON adapter above.
software.dependencies: Meshroom/AliceVision bundled executable and pipeline resources; NVIDIA CUDA recommended for full reconstruction per official release notes.

steps.action: Calibrate the board-image subset with OpenCV calibrateCamera/projectPoints using the board inner-corner count, measured square size and unit; retain the per-image residuals.

Adapt the calibration JSON to COLMAP explicitly. For an OpenCV five-coefficient calibration result, use COLMAP FULL_OPENCV parameters [fx, fy, cx+0.5, cy+0.5, k1, k2, p1, p2, k3, 0, 0, 0]. The +0.5 shifts OpenCV pixel-center coordinates to COLMAP’s corner-based convention. Supply these during feature_extractor with --ImageReader.camera_model FULL_OPENCV --ImageReader.camera_params <comma-separated values> and --ImageReader.single_camera 1 only if every image has identical sensor/crop/focus settings. Read the stored camera back through pycolmap.Database.read_camera and compare width, height, model and every parameter before mapping; choose whether bundle adjustment may refine intrinsics. Never edit the binary SQLite camera parameter blob by hand.
Run COLMAP feature_extractor, matcher and mapper on the photo set, producing database.db and a sparse/0 camera model with sparse points.

Bridge the COLMAP sparse result to OpenMVS: run colmap image_undistorter --image_path <images> --input_path sparse/0 --output_path dense --output_type COLMAP, then InterfaceCOLMAP -i dense -o scene.mvs --image-folder dense/images. Run DensifyPointCloud scene.mvs and ReconstructMesh scene_dense.mvs. This explicit importer consumes undistorted images, sparse camera poses and sparse cloud.

Set the reconstruction’s metric frame/scale from distributed measured controls, reserve independent control lengths, then remodel selected features in OCS with dimensions labeled by evidence and read back the CAD revision.

code.entrypoint: OpenCV findChessboardCornersSB, calibrateCamera and projectPoints: supply board object coordinates, detected image corners and image dimensions; retain intrinsics, distortion, poses and reprojection residuals.

outputs.representation: Metric-anchored camera solution, dense surface reference and constrained CAD interpretation.
outputs.dimensional_status: Metric only where tied to explicit controls/sensor calibration; learned visual surfaces and view-synthesis products remain inferred or appearance representations.
outputs.editable_cad_dependency: OCS remodeling is a separate feature-interpretation stage requiring explicit dimensions, coordinate frame, constraints and readback.

workflows.checks: Pixel reprojection residuals; registered image fraction; withheld scale-control length error; mesh-to-cloud regional distances; OCS readback and independent feature dimensions. COLMAP camera DB readback: model name, image width/height and parameter values equal the adapter values after principal point conversion; verify whether bundle-adjustment refinement is enabled. Check COLMAP sparse reprojection and camera model before OpenMVS conversion.
workflows.failure_recovery: If calibration residuals cluster by image edge, verify lens/focus and corner detections; recapture target views if insufficient. If SfM separates into components, improve overlap/mask moving objects. If dense mesh is incomplete, adjust image coverage/lighting or use calibrated depth. If control residuals vary spatially, retain warp evidence and rebuild with more distributed controls rather than only uniform scale. If COLMAP intrinsics differ from calibration unexpectedly, inspect parameter ordering, OpenCV-to-COLMAP +0.5 px principal-point conversion, image resize/crop and bundle-adjustment refinement. Reinitialize the database with corrected feature_extractor options or use pycolmap.Database.update_camera, then read back the camera. If InterfaceCOLMAP rejects the scene, confirm image_undistorter produced COLMAP dense workspace with matching undistorted images and camera records.

effort.human_reason: Full measured reconstruction plus semantic CAD remodeling has several interpretation and validation stages.
effort.setup_reason: Requires camera calibration, photogrammetry, MVS and OCS adapters.
effort.compute_reason: Dense MVS is CPU/RAM intensive; GPU acceleration is backend dependent; no universal minimum is established.

resources.cpu: OpenMVG/MVS supports CPU processing; image count/resolution affect time.
resources.gpu: MVS acceleration varies by build; no universal GPU minimum was documented.
resources.ram: Dense depth maps raise RAM use with image size and camera count; no universal minimum.
resources.storage: Keep images, sparse scene, dense maps and mesh; storage grows with source resolution and MVS outputs.
resources.scaling_drivers: Image count/resolution, depth-map resolution, overlap and dense reconstruction parameters.
resources.variants: Sparse-only reconstruction lowers cost but omits a dense surface; metric CAD still requires controls and OCS interpretation.

workflows.name: Video and RGB-D to registered metric scene
workflows.output_scope: Registered RGB photo-derived cloud and sensor-depth cloud, fused depth mesh and a checked source-to-target transform.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Video frames overlap with RGB-D capture or share enough geometry; depth calibration, RGB-depth extrinsics and sensor units are known; motion/rolling-shutter errors are controlled.

inputs.format_and_quality: Original video with timestamps and camera metadata; sufficient parallax and sharp frames.
RGB/depth frames and camera intrinsics/extrinsics; raw depth scale/range stated.
Independent control distances/targets and frame coordinates; withheld controls retained.

workflows.reference_points: Depth sensor calibration provides per-frame camera intrinsics, depth scale and RGB-depth extrinsics. COLMAP estimates RGB camera poses; depth odometry or sensor trajectory estimates range poses. FPFH/RANSAC establishes a coarse transform between distinct source/target clouds; ICP refines only with same-scale clouds and a good initial transform. Withheld dimensions test drift.

software.name: Open3D
software.role_and_api: RGB-D odometry, global registration, registration_icp, TSDF integration

steps.action: Extract selected frames preserving source timestamps and frame indices.
Estimate RGB camera poses/cloud with COLMAP; estimate depth trajectory/cloud from calibrated frames or sensor SLAM.
Use global registration for coarse alignment if needed, followed by Open3D registration_icp using explicit initial 4x4 and model-unit threshold.
Integrate depth frames through TSDF with calibrated trajectory; compare loop closure and independent controls.

code.entrypoint: Open3D registration_icp(source, target, max_correspondence_distance, init, estimation_method): provide source/target clouds in compatible units and a source-to-target initialization; inspect transformation, fitness and inlier_rmse.

outputs.representation: Registered RGB photo-derived cloud and sensor-depth cloud, fused depth mesh and a checked source-to-target transform.
outputs.dimensional_status: Metric only where tied to explicit controls/sensor calibration; learned visual surfaces and view-synthesis products remain inferred or appearance representations.
outputs.editable_cad_dependency: No new CAD in this workflow.

workflows.checks: Timestamp and sharpness coverage; RGB/depth alignment; source-to-target transform direction; ICP fitness/inlier RMSE; loop closure; held-out range controls; TSDF mesh-to-point-cloud residuals.
workflows.failure_recovery: If visual odometry drifts, add loop closure/targets or use sensor SLAM; if ICP fails, check units, initial transform, overlap and symmetry. Do not change threshold to hide a systematic residual. If RGB/depth edges disagree, check synchronization and extrinsics.

effort.human_reason: Combines two sensing paths and frame alignment, but stops at a registered metric scene.
effort.setup_reason: Requires video extraction, sensor calibration and reconstruction/registration tools.
effort.compute_reason: Dense cloud registration and TSDF integrate many samples; compute scales with frame count, image dimensions and voxel density.

resources.cpu: Frame extraction, Open3D ICP and TSDF have CPU paths.
resources.gpu: GPU use depends on selected SfM/SLAM backend; no requirement for core Open3D example.
resources.ram: RAM scales with frame count, point count and voxel volume.
resources.storage: Original video, extracted frames, depth, cloud and mesh storage scale with duration/resolution.
resources.scaling_drivers: Frame count/resolution, point density, TSDF voxel length and cloud overlap.
resources.variants: RGB-D-only route removes photo SfM comparison; photo-only route loses sensor depth metric input.

workflows.name: Existing CAD aligned to calibrated photos
workflows.output_scope: Camera pose linking a known CAD revision to photo views and pixel reprojection report.
workflows.comparison_conditions: CAD datum and units known; visible unique CAD landmarks; calibrated camera; pixel correspondences identified in the supplied measurement set.

inputs.format_and_quality: Native editable CAD source and revision identifier.
Calibration and object image set with stable camera/lens settings.
CAD/world 3D point IDs and corresponding 2D pixel coordinates; units explicit.

workflows.reference_points: PnP uses labeled pairs (X,Y,Z) in CAD/world frame and (u,v) pixels plus K/distortion. OpenCV outputs object/world-to-camera. Camera axes X-right Y-down Z-forward. A separate calibration target is required for K/distortion unless a documented calibration exists. Held-out CAD landmarks check pose, not hidden geometry.

DXF/SVG/PDF-derived linework with known scale, datums and drawing revision.

Segment planes/clusters and record indices, thresholds and fit residuals.

workflows.name: Photos, learned depth and view-synthesis comparison
workflows.output_scope: Separate SfM and DA3 camera/depth/cloud estimates plus Gaussian view-synthesis scene and control residual comparison.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Multi-view photos with overlap; independent dimensions/targets; selected DA3 and Splatfacto variants and model terms reviewed; same photo set used for comparisons.

inputs.format_and_quality: Original overlapping JPEG/PNG photos with camera metadata and static scene.
Measured control lengths/points with fit versus withheld labels.

workflows.reference_points: DA3 depth/pose is a model estimate and can provide metric variant but requires physical controls. COLMAP scale remains arbitrary absent controls. Splat scene optimizes novel-view appearance; it is not a mesh. Similarity alignment for comparing cloud estimates must be reported separately from metric controls.

steps.action: Run COLMAP sparse reconstruction and preserve component/camera metadata.
Run DA3 multi-view or streaming inference; preserve metric/relative model name, confidence, poses and output formats.
Train Gaussian view-synthesis scene from photos and known/estimated camera solution.
Register estimate clouds with controls; compare withheld lengths, regional residuals and pose consistency.

code.entrypoint: Open3D registration_icp(source, target, max_correspondence_distance, init, estimation_method): provide source/target clouds in compatible units and a source-to-target initialization; inspect transformation, fitness and inlier_rmse.

outputs.representation: Separate SfM and DA3 camera/depth/cloud estimates plus Gaussian view-synthesis scene and control residual comparison.
outputs.dimensional_status: Metric only where tied to explicit controls/sensor calibration; learned visual surfaces and view-synthesis products remain inferred or appearance representations.
outputs.editable_cad_dependency: No new CAD in this workflow.

workflows.checks: Compare DA3 metric depth against independent control points; COLMAP reprojection errors; inter-estimate transform; regional cloud residuals; novel-view coverage separately from surface quality.
workflows.failure_recovery: If DA3 and SfM disagree, check camera metadata, moving objects, lens distortion and scale/control definition. Report two estimates separately; do not average without a stated statistical model. If splat render artifacts occur, revise capture coverage; do not substitute splat appearance for dimensional evidence.

effort.human_reason: Reviewing multiple model outputs and allocating controls requires engineering judgment.
effort.setup_reason: Combines reconstruction, learned model and CUDA scene training.
effort.compute_reason: DA3 streaming reports <12 GB GPU memory; Splatfacto docs list ~6 GB default and ~12 GB big; runtime scales with views/resolution.

resources.cpu: Image preparation and sparse SfM use CPU.
resources.gpu: DA3 Streaming reports below 12 GB memory; Nerfstudio lists about 6 GB for default Splatfacto and 12 GB for Splatfacto-big in source report.
resources.ram: Model and reconstruction data scale with view count/resolution; no universal system-RAM minimum.
resources.scaling_drivers: Image resolution/count, chosen DA3 variant, Gaussian scene complexity.
resources.variants: Omit Gaussian branch for lower compute; omit DA3 branch to compare conventional SfM alone.

workflows.name: Gaussian context, independent mesh and CAD remodel
workflows.output_scope: Gaussian PLY context, independently generated MVS mesh/cloud and editable CAD aligned to source evidence.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Overlapping photos, camera solution, independent control points; MVS mesh and measured dimensions available for selected CAD features.

inputs.format_and_quality: Static, overlapping multi-view photographs.
Control lengths/points and dimensions with units and withheld checks.

workflows.reference_points: Gaussian scene is a view-synthesis representation. REC-17 MVS creates a separate mesh/cloud from photos and camera poses. Controls define scale/checks. CAD features are rebuilt from measurements and explicit interpretation; splat geometry is not assumed to be an analytic surface.

steps.action: Estimate camera poses using COLMAP.
Train and export Gaussian PLY from Splatfacto for appearance context.
Generate dense point cloud and mesh independently using OpenMVS; use measured controls for scale.
Remodel selected features in OCS from the dense surface and dimensions; preserve separate splat, mesh, CAD layers.
Compare CAD with source cloud and withheld dimensions.

code.entrypoint: Open3D registration_icp(source, target, max_correspondence_distance, init, estimation_method): provide source/target clouds in compatible units and a source-to-target initialization; inspect transformation, fitness and inlier_rmse.

outputs.representation: Gaussian PLY context, independently generated MVS mesh/cloud and editable CAD aligned to source evidence.
outputs.dimensional_status: Metric only where tied to explicit controls/sensor calibration; learned visual surfaces and view-synthesis products remain inferred or appearance representations.
outputs.editable_cad_dependency: OCS remodeling is a separate feature-interpretation stage requiring explicit dimensions, coordinate frame, constraints and readback.

workflows.checks: Novel view rendering; MVS coverage/mesh completeness; control residuals; source-to-CAD distances; CAD feature dimensions; representation transform consistency.
workflows.failure_recovery: If Splatfacto mesh extraction is requested, its current FAQ says unsupported; use separate MVS or calibrated depth TSDF. If MVS incomplete, improve photos or add sensor depth. If CAD fit to scan deforms beyond controls, revise alignment/feature assumptions.

effort.human_reason: Requires managing three representations and remodeling semantic features.
effort.setup_reason: Three software stacks including GPU scene training and OCS modeling.
effort.compute_reason: Dense stereo plus Gaussian training and CAD comparison; image count/resolution/cloud density drive memory and compute.

resources.cpu: COLMAP/OpenMVS and cloud comparison are CPU-capable.
resources.gpu: Splatfacto uses CUDA GPU; source report lists ~6 GB default and ~12 GB big. MVS acceleration varies by build.
resources.ram: Dense MVS plus Gaussian training can raise memory; no universal system-RAM floor.
resources.storage: Store original photos, dense maps, mesh, checkpoint, Gaussian PLY and CAD.
resources.scaling_drivers: Image resolution/count, scene complexity, MVS depth density and mesh size.
resources.variants: Omit scene training for a lower-cost mesh-to-CAD path; omit CAD for visual-only deliverable.

workflows.name: 3D-anchored sketch and CAD edit comparison
workflows.output_scope: Calculated screen-stroke anchors, interpreted constrained CAD feature and revision-bound comparison report.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Existing calibrated camera solution and mesh/CAD target; screen strokes belong to the image associated with that camera; user supplies feature interpretation and dimensions.

inputs.format_and_quality: Image plus pixel-space strokes in a documented image coordinate system.
Intrinsics/distortion and camera pose tied to exact view and coordinate frame.
Selected raycast surface with transform and revision.
Physical dimensions/datum controls and explicit intended feature interpretation.

workflows.reference_points: Pixels map to normalized camera rays with K/distortion inverse, transformed into world by camera pose; ray intersection yields calculated 3D anchors against selected mesh. The mesh and camera are reference evidence. Anchors carry the uncertainty of calibration, pose, mesh and hit selection; they are not independent measurements. Independent dimension controls check CAD.

software.name: Blender Python API
software.dependencies: Blender bpy; signature version checked at implementation

software.name: OpenCV
software.licence_scope: Apache-2.0 for OpenCV >=4.5 (including current 4.x); older releases retain their release-specific BSD-3-Clause terms
software.role_and_api: projectPoints/PnP for pose calibration or reprojection

steps.action: Map stroke pixels through image calibration to camera rays; record camera, hit object and face/triangle IDs.
Store ray-hit anchors and projection residual context in measurement-set as calculated anchors.
Ask for/consume explicit sketch interpretation: surface curve, projected profile or datum-plane sketch; apply dimensions/constraints in OCS.
Read back CAD revision and compare with same mesh and independent controls.

code.path: Blender Python Console (native bpy API; no project script)
code.entrypoint: depsgraph = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get(); hit, location, normal, face_index, obj, matrix = bpy.context.scene.ray_cast(depsgraph, origin, direction); origin/direction are world-space rays computed from the calibrated camera and stroke pixel.

outputs.representation: Calculated screen-stroke anchors, interpreted constrained CAD feature and revision-bound comparison report.
outputs.dimensional_status: Metric only where tied to explicit controls/sensor calibration; learned visual surfaces and view-synthesis products remain inferred or appearance representations.
outputs.editable_cad_dependency: OCS remodeling is a separate feature-interpretation stage requiring explicit dimensions, coordinate frame, constraints and readback.

workflows.checks: Reproject calculated anchors into original image; flag missed/occluded rays; check camera calibration/view identity; inspect hit distribution; verify OCS constraints and independent physical dimensions.
workflows.failure_recovery: For ambiguous rays, require selected target surface or user selection; preserve multiple hit candidates. For sketch-plane ambiguity, stop at anchors until interpreted. If visible mesh is poorly reconstructed, do not convert anchor hits into physical dimensions.

effort.setup_reason: Camera projection, raycast adapter and OCS session.
effort.compute_reason: Raycasting a small stroke set and CAD checks are CPU-light; high-resolution source mesh increases cost.

software.role_and_api: ns-process-data, ns-train splatfacto, Gaussian PLY export

steps.action: Run COLMAP pose recovery or import the supplied camera solution and preserve image-to-camera mapping.

Inspect held-out novel views and preserve the checkpoint, processed transforms and original photo set. Any mesh must come from a separate documented geometry extraction step.

workflows.name: Single-image mesh proxy and evidence-based CAD remodel
workflows.output_scope: Learned single-view mesh proxy, followed by constrained CAD built from supplied independent dimensions and measured data.
workflows.comparison_conditions: One image suffices for a visual proxy. Full CAD path additionally requires measured dimensions, drawing views or other evidence for unseen geometry and scale.

inputs.format_and_quality: Single object photograph with clean silhouette/lighting; input set contains one selected view.
Independent dimensions, target frame and observed landmarks for CAD authoring/checks.
Part identity/features and output scope; no dimensions are inferred from brief.

workflows.reference_points: Image-to-3D models infer backside/occluded surfaces from priors and do not establish physical scale. Measurements provide dimensional evidence. Additional views are required to compare unseen geometry; surface proxy is not editable parametric CAD.

software.name: TRELLIS.2-4B
software.licence_scope: MIT repository/model card per existing report

software.name: SAM 3D Objects
software.licence_scope: Custom Meta SAM terms per existing report

software.name: OCS
software.role_and_api: constrained CAD remodeling using measured dimensions

steps.action: For the TripoSR branch, run the upstream documented command `python run.py <single-image> --output-dir <output-folder>` to create a mesh proxy; alternatively run the selected TRELLIS.2 or SAM 3D model under its own documented environment and checkpoint terms. Retain model revision and image provenance.
Measure/control source dimensions independently; compare visible silhouette across any extra views.
Rebuild selected features with constraints in OCS using supplied dimensions; label unseen geometry as inferred.
Read back CAD and compare to independent measurements, not proxy surface alone.

code.path: TripoSR CLI (native tool entrypoint; no project script)

outputs.representation: Learned single-view mesh proxy, followed by constrained CAD built from supplied independent dimensions and measured data.
outputs.dimensional_status: Metric only where tied to explicit controls/sensor calibration; learned visual surfaces and view-synthesis products remain inferred or appearance representations.
outputs.editable_cad_dependency: OCS remodeling is a separate feature-interpretation stage requiring explicit dimensions, coordinate frame, constraints and readback.

workflows.checks: Source silhouette; model/revision/weight terms; dimension comparisons; CAD constraints and units; separate proxy-vs-CAD residual from physical measurement residual.
workflows.failure_recovery: If inferred backside is inconsistent with extra views, retain proxy as visual placeholder and remodel manually. If critical dimensions are absent, stop at mesh proxy; do not scale from image appearance. If model terms exclude intended use, switch model before generating deliverable.

effort.human_reason: Single-view proxy is easy, but full measured CAD remodeling is hard because unseen shape requires independent evidence and feature decisions.
effort.setup_reason: Learned model setup, checkpoint terms and OCS CAD environment.
effort.compute_reason: GPU requirements vary sharply: TripoSR ~6 GB, TRELLIS.2-4B >=24 GB, SAM 3D >=32 GB per existing source reports.

resources.cpu: Image preparation and OCS readback use CPU; inference backend may use GPU.
resources.gpu: TripoSR ~6 GB; TRELLIS.2-4B >=24 GB; SAM 3D Objects >=32 GB NVIDIA per existing report.
resources.ram: Model-specific VRAM plus point/mesh processing; no common system-RAM minimum.
resources.storage: Model checkpoints, source images, generated textures/mesh and CAD revisions.
resources.scaling_drivers: Model family, texture/resolution settings, single-view ambiguity and CAD feature count.
resources.variants: Proxy-only route has low human effort and GPU inference; full measured CAD requires more evidence and high human interpretation.

ranking_notes.human_effort_and_compute_are_independent: Scores use contract scales 1-5, conditions and reasons above. Equal numeric scores tie. They are not runtimes, hardware benchmarks, accuracy scores or measured human action counts.
ranking_notes.task_granularity: operation_stage_count counts listed reference stages only; it does not count clicks, processing jobs or elapsed time.
ranking_notes.rank_order: Lower tie rank means lower effort/compute; stage_count_order sorts listed stage counts ascending then workflow ID.
